solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leaving first university, melancholy man beaming

indicators.note: the first of the two university letters in the melancholy word goes away

parts.note: rueful means sorrowful, melancholy
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A sad man is radiant after quitting his degree course.
explanation.walkthrough: RUEFUL has two Us; 'Leaving first' drops only the first, giving REFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Refulgent is a literary synonym for shining brightly, radiating light.

clue.text: Bear forward: game on!

indicators.note: in a down clue, the game sits on top of the forward word

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
pert means cheeky, forward

explanation.surface: A cry urging a bear onward, as if the match is starting.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Bear is a long-running British children's cartoon character.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous cartoon bear in checked trousers is called by this first name.

clue.text: In illness, one poor student swallowing at first only a little liquid

parts.note: flu is an illness
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the poor student takes in a letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a dunce is a poor student

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A sick student, struggling, manages to drink just a drop of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The O from 'only' goes inside DUNCE after its D, giving DOUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fluid ounce is a small measure of volume for liquids.

clue.text: Looking up pet rodent, avoiding first dry old textbook

indicators.note: the opening letter of the rodent's name is dropped
in a down clue, reading upward turns the pet rodent backwards

parts.note: a gerbil is a rodent kept as a pet
TT, teetotal, means not drinking, dry

explanation.surface: Someone checks on a pet gerbil while skipping a dull, outdated schoolbook.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversed GERBIL is LIBREG; dropping the G that began GERBIL leaves LIBRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the book containing the words of an opera, so a text book in a punning sense.

clue.text: Say, soak to soften wader

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as 'say' does
to ret is to soak flax or hemp to soften the fibres

explanation.surface: Advice on soaking something to make it softer, oddly ending with a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a heron-like bird that wades in shallow water.

clue.text: More peaceful path for medieval conqueror

parts.note: tamer means gentler, more peaceful
a lane is a narrow path or road

explanation.surface: A calmer route chosen by a warlord of the Middle Ages.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamerlane, or Timur, was the fourteenth-century Turco-Mongol conqueror.

clue.text: Fish commonly taking wrong direction

indicators.note: in common, dropped-aitch speech the opening letter of the fish is not sounded

parts.note: a herring is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish, in everyday speech, is heading the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' signals the dropped H of colloquial speech, as in 'erring for herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Erring means straying or going astray, as one who takes a wrong course.

clue.text: Vehicle is large, in my opinion

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
IMO is the texting abbreviation for in my opinion

explanation.surface: Someone offers a view that a car is big.
explanation.definitionFit: A limo, short for limousine, is a large luxury car.

clue.text: Use staff meanly? Make little of losing pounds

indicators.note: the pounds abbreviation is taken out of the phrase for playing down

parts.note: to underplay is to downplay, make little of
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (libra)

explanation.surface: Treating employees stingily means playing down the loss of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay workers less than they deserve is to treat staff stingily.

clue.text: Charge soldier to retreat into Scottish island

indicators.note: the reversed soldier goes inside the island's name

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the soldier abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is accused for withdrawing to a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to formally charge someone in court.

clue.text: With pressure, burden tradesman

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
to lumber someone is to burden them

explanation.surface: A workman weighed down and under stress.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumber is a skilled tradesman fitting pipes and water systems.

clue.text: Pub welcomes Round Table, at last united

indicators.note: the pub takes the round letter in, holding it inside

parts.note: an inn is a pub
O is round in shape

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A pub hosts members of the Round Table, finally bringing them together.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things in one are combined, joined as a single whole.

clue.text: Dog looking ashamed, having fouled street

parts.note: red-faced, someone ashamed looks red

indicators.note: fouled means messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog looks guilty after messing on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: The red setter, or Irish setter, is a breed of gun dog.

clue.text: Parts of body that may be found in field

definitions.text: Parts of body that may be found in field

parts.words: Parts of body that may be found in field
parts.note: limbs plus a mouth's edge are body parts, and together they name a cricket fielding position

explanation.surface: Body parts turning up in a meadow, as if from a grisly discovery.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, leg slip is a fielder placed close behind the batsman on the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: This cricket fielding position is literally made of two body-part words.

clue.text: Check last piece of editorial copy

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word editorial is used

parts.note: an imitation is a copy

explanation.surface: A sub-editor reviews the final part of a newspaper leader's text.
explanation.definitionFit: A check is a restriction or curb, something that holds back.

clue.text: Electrical inventor not needing most of site's laboratory

indicators.note: most of the two words is discarded, leaving a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: An inventor works without needing much of the site's lab.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla pioneered alternating-current electrical systems.

clue.text: Replace leather worn by individual: not on!

indicators.note: the leather goes around the shortened individual, as clothing does on a wearer

parts.note: suede is a kind of leather

indicators.note: the word on is not included in the individual

parts.note: a person is an individual

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take off their leather jacket and swap it.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede is to take the place of, to supplant.

clue.text: Rude order to servant to leave fruit

parts.note: a man is a manservant
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A curt command dismissing a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rude order to servant' reads as 'Man, go!', a brusque dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a tropical stone fruit.

clue.text: Slander about one's not put straight

indicators.note: the slander word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to malign is to slander
one's is I'S, I being one

explanation.surface: Slandering someone means not setting the record straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Misaligned things are out of line, not set correctly in position.

clue.text: Doubtful apostle could be so familiar as a soldier?

definitions.text: Doubtful apostle could be so familiar as a soldier?

parts.words: Doubtful apostle could be so familiar as a soldier?
parts.note: Doubting Thomas's pet name is also the nickname for a British private soldier

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the doubting disciple could pass as a soldier by a nickname.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Atkins is the traditional nickname for a British private.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the familiar form of Thomas and slang for a British soldier.

clue.text: Impetuousness may finally wear me out — time up!

indicators.note: up as in disordered, so the letters are jumbled
the final letters of the four words are taken

explanation.surface: A cry that rashness will exhaust the speaker, and time has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes YRET from the ends of may, wear, me, out; 'up' mixes these with TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Temerity is rash boldness, a reckless impetuous nerve.

clue.text: Annoy English deputy in US made to return

indicators.note: returning means reading the joined pieces backwards

parts.note: veep is American slang for vice-president

explanation.surface: An English vice-president in America is irritated at being sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: To peeve is to irritate or vex.

clue.text: Tower with record inscribed in column

indicators.note: the record is carved into the column, so it goes inside

parts.note: a stele is an upright stone pillar
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A tower with an account carved into its pillar.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a church tower with a spire.

clue.text: Dish containing a relish

indicators.note: the dish holds the single letter inside it

parts.note: a plate is a dish

explanation.surface: A plate holding a pickle or chutney.
explanation.definitionFit: Palate means taste, a liking or relish for something.

clue.text: Grab and beat up in school

indicators.note: the reversed beat goes inside the school
in a down clue, up means the word is read upward, backwards

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: Bullying at school: seizing things and beating pupils up.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch is to seize quickly, to grab.

clue.text: Make fuss and prepare to strike blow on ear

parts.note: one raises a hand or stick before striking

indicators.note: heard by the ear, the word for a stroke sounds like the biblical name

parts.note: a cane is a stroke of the cane, a blow

explanation.surface: Kicking up a fuss and getting ready to hit someone round the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise Cain is an idiom for causing an uproar or trouble.

clue.text: Problem children

definitions.meaning: a matter of concern, a problem
... means offspring, as in died without ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a contested matter and a person's offspring.

clue.text: Such lite food served here?

parts.note: low-calorie fare is ..., and a pub serving food is a neighbourhood boozer

explanation.surface: Asking whether diet food is on the menu here.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as LO-CAL it describes the diet food; read whole, it is a British word for one's nearby pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub near home, where meals are often served, is called this in Britain.

clue.text: Run into youngster, 14

indicators.note: the run abbreviation goes inside the youngster

parts.note: a cub is a young animal or a junior scout
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A cross-reference clue: dash into a young scout.
explanation.walkthrough: '14' points to the answer at 14-down, meaning a check or restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: A curb is a restraint, a restriction holding something back.

clue.text: If wearing small skirt, it will ride up in the cold

definitions.text: it will ride up in the cold

indicators.note: the word if is inside the small skirt, as a wearer is inside clothes

parts.note: a kilt is a Scottish skirt

explanation.surface: A short kilt rides up on a chilly day.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairlift or tow carries skiers uphill in the snowy mountains.

clue.text: Writhed as tragedy unfolded

indicators.note: unfolded suggests the letters opening out into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone squirmed as a disaster played out.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyrated means twisted or whirled about, much as writhing does.

clue.text: Thoroughly European, envy rich criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A European is thoroughly jealous of a wealthy crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Every inch is an idiom meaning entirely, in every respect.
